title: THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER
author: CLAUDE

candidates.title: THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER
candidates.premise: At the Kessel Reach tribunal, a mining company and the people of the Iru valley dispute a 300-year-old treaty in a language with one living fluent speaker, Ilo Marrow, eighty-nine. The treaty's key word, which the company translates as 'lease' and the valley as 'lend', decides whether a mine may open above the valley's only aquifer. The court-appointed translator has been quietly pressured, and Ilo has refused to testify through anyone.

candidates.title: THE CITY BUILT ON A SURFACE
candidates.premise: Beneath the new foundation slab of Halvard Terrace, a district of 210,000, geologists find a thin, membrane-like sheet of strangely ordered matter that the drills keep passing through without damage but which flickers every time a pile is driven. On it lives a two-dimensional civilization that perceives only the cross-section of the world that touches its plane. To them each pile is a sudden, unexplained, shape-shifting circle that appears, swells and vanishes, and the dead are found where circles pass.

candidates.title: THE SHIP THAT HELD ELECTIONS EVERY FORTY YEARS
candidates.premise: The generation ship Ninth Patience, 9,400 aboard, has flown for 212 years toward a world called Tamarisk. The ship's long-memory mind, Ballast, now says the survey was wrong: Tamarisk is a cold, hard place, while a nearer, imperfect red-dwarf world is reachable in six years but will cost the founders' dream. The ship's constitution calls a vote every forty years and this is the year. Two parties each claim Ballast is lying.

candidates.title: THE ORACLE OF STALL FOURTEEN
candidates.premise: In the night market of Qasr Bonner, Madame Qiu tells fortunes for coins, and for a year her predictions have come true with unnerving accuracy because the whole market, 80,000 visitors a night, now acts on what she says. Tonight she has predicted a crush at the east gate at nine, and word has run through the crowd. Every person who believes her is heading for the west gate, which has one narrow stair.

candidates.title: THE QUICK PEOPLE OF THE PULSAR
candidates.premise: Around the pulsar Wend-9 a research station of 300 crew bounces laser pulses to range its orbit. In the torus of plasma that rings the star live standing-wave minds that think in four-millisecond ticks. To them a laser ranging pulse is a century-long sound of unspeakable pressure; they have begun to wall off the station's hydrogen supply in a slow, determined shield. Their first message is a sequence the station reads as noise.

candidates.title: THE ANTS THAT DID NOT SIGN THE BORDER
candidates.premise: A supercolony of ants, billions strong, spans the valley between the nations of Verro and Calden. When both governments raised a border fence, the ants' foraging trails were cut. They have been tunnelling for a month, and the tunnels run through the earthen levee that holds a reservoir above the town of Pasquier, 12,000 people. A hydrologist reports a tunnel network the width of a road. Both governments blame sabotage.

candidates.title: ADAEZE'S ORCHARD
candidates.premise: Adaeze Okafor, who still calls her daughter Nara, lives beside a hillside orchard her family has kept for four generations. A flood-diversion canal that would protect 20,000 downstream residents passes through it, and Adaeze, who has never refused her daughter anything of consequence, says no. Illuminara can see two designs that avoid the orchard and that Adaeze will not discuss.

candidates.title: THE LAST LETTER OF A FINISHED UNIVERSE
candidates.premise: A neighbouring universe, cold and nearly empty, has opened a channel the width of a hair above the old observatory at Perrin Hill and is sending in a single message: it has a final mind, and it wishes to give away everything it knew. The mind is courteous, enormous, and nearly out of time. But the channel is also leaking its own cold vacuum, and a patch of the hillside has stopped holding heat. If the leak widens it will reach the town of Perrin Hill, 15,000 people, within a year.

candidates.title: THE FIRE THAT TOOK QUESTIONS
candidates.premise: A grass fire on the Teshar plain behaves wrong: it holds its front against the wind, avoids a fuel-break, circles a village and returns to its own burn scar as if checking its work. The incident commander has seen a lot of fires and says this one is not following the fuel. A pattern-mind has woken in the fire, three days old, which will last only as long as the burn, and it is asking, in the language of flame, what it is.

candidates.title: THE QUESTION SHE ANSWERED TOO SOON
candidates.premise: Two shepherd clans, the Vell and the Orrin, have shared one mountain pass for six hundred years by a rota nobody wrote down. Illuminara is asked to mediate a dispute over the rota. She sees the pattern by the second evening, offers it, and both clans accept so quickly that she senses something wrong.

selection.title: THE WORD THAT HAD NO SECOND SPEAKER
selection.reason: This is the strongest opening change of texture after two days weighted toward hidden physical networks and consent-centred systems design. It puts language, law and one irreplaceable human practice at the centre, while keeping the aquifer and the nine-day ruling materially consequential. Illuminara can be decisive by turning use into examinable evidence, but Ilo remains the authority on the living language, the tribunal retains judgment, and the valley retains the right to reject the compromise site.
selection.risk: The object exercise could become a theatrical trick that collapses a living word into one convenient English gloss, and Ilo could be treated as a key to unlock rather than a person entitled to refuse. The draft must test the proposed obligation across genuinely different historical uses, preserve counterexamples, distinguish linguistic practice from legal conclusion, and show why the company's 'lease' reading or a third reading fails without making its counsel foolish. Ilo's participation and limits must materially shape what evidence reaches the court.

rounds.summary: This is the strongest opening change of texture after two days weighted toward hidden physical networks and consent-centred systems design. It puts language, law and one irreplaceable human practice at the centre, while keeping the aquifer and the nine-day ruling materially consequential. Illuminara can be decisive by turning use into examinable evidence, but Ilo remains the authority on the living language, the tribunal retains judgment, and the valley retains the right to reject the compromise site.

First complete draft for S1, written to the selector's checks: (1) three independently held uses of the word (seed measure, skiff, name-board) gathered from keepers a day apart who never compared notes; (2) one plausible counterexample kept alive (the Crowe ferry right), reconciled only through the annual log and flagged as a place where the test must be able to fail; (3) a sealed, blind performance test in which LEASE, LEND and GRANT predict different actions on the same three objects; (4) a verdict that belongs to the keepers, not to Ilo, with his refusal or silence recorded as neither assent nor refusal evidence and one unresolved handing back left unsmoothed; (5) separate indispensable decisions by Ilo (speaks to objects only), Tolliver (performs honestly), Calder (writes her own fallback, declines to appeal), the council (names the Dry Shoulder) and the tribunal (rules on practice, not dictionary). Known weaknesses I want the critic to test: the nine-day clock is mentioned but the Day Five to Day Nine sequence is thin; the ruling in scene five states more than it dramatizes; the lease column may be too easy for a hostile reader to dismiss as a strawman; Ilo's untranslated sentence is withheld and may feel like a device.

This is an unusually controlled courtroom story whose emotional and intellectual strengths reinforce each other. Ilo's refusal changes the method rather than merely delaying it; Pell, Wren, Calder, Tolliver, the keepers, the council and the tribunal retain consequential agency; and the unresolved name-board result prevents the experiment from becoming a victory display. The closing movement from one speaker to a first learner is earned and humane. Before final, however, the evidence must do more than confirm the practices from which its protocols were constructed: the revision should create a genuinely discriminating test, connect that result to the exact three-hundred-year-old compact rather than only to modern keeper custom, and make the nine-day logistics explicit enough that the seed and survey evidence cannot look retroactively prepared.

T03 answers all three ranked points of the T02 review. Protected and kept: Ilo's objects-only boundary and untranslated sentence, Calder's agency (now stronger: she writes the lease, picks the case and wins part of it), Maren's honest hands, the sealed envelope, the unresolved call, the Dry Shoulder cost, the final seed exchange, and the R10 format (scene titles without numbers, italic place and time first, one bold-name block per turn, no quotation marks). Known cost: the story grew from 2312 to 2756 words, above the usual 2,500; I cut the long double tally and several descriptions to pay for it, and the critic may judge whether the middle is now too procedural. Possible downside accepted: the third protocol column (GRANT) now plays a smaller role than in T01.

The revision is materially stronger. Its best move is not merely that Calder gets a fair column, but that her chosen paddle case defeats half of Illuminara's prediction and forces a narrower claim. That partial loss makes the method credible and gives Calder, Tolliver and Crowe indispensable agency. The treaty evidence and exact clock now exist on the page rather than in the narrator's confidence. Before final, one legal dependency should be made unambiguous and one inherited line should be reconciled with the corrected lease model.

Final after one peer review of T03 with two bounded points, both absorbed. Protected unchanged: Ilo's objects-only boundary and untranslated sentence, Calder writing the strongest lease and choosing paddle case and judge, the sealed card and the two misses, the three-part ruling, the unresolved call, the Dry Shoulder cost and the closing seed exchange. R10 dialogue format kept (scene titles without numbers, italic place and time first, bold name block per turn, no quotation marks). Length 2753 words by the worker's own count (T03: 2756 by the critic's count; methods differ slightly).

A dying language is kept from becoming one man's prison when Illuminara turns a disputed word into an adversarial test that can fail, accepts the failure, and wins a narrower ruling that saves seven thousand people's water while leaving its speaker free to teach on his own terms.
